cards.text: Meet Noah, friend: a righteous man, blameless in his generation, who walked with God. He has three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth. Blameless, baker, and I can't get through one batch without flour on my mustache.
Now the rest of the earth? Whew. God looks it over and sees it's corrupt, because all living creatures on the earth had corrupted their ways.

cards.question: Besides being corrupt in the sight of God, what is the earth full of?

cards.text: Then God speaks to Noah, and it's heavy: "The end of all living creatures has come before Me, because through them the earth is full of violence."

cards.question: God tells Noah the end has come. What does God say He will destroy?
Destruction is coming, but God has a plan for Noah. What does God tell Noah to make for himself?

cards.text: Then God hands Noah the building plans: gopher wood, rooms, pitch inside and out, a roof, a door in the side, three decks, and 300 cubits long. Friend, I needed three tries to put together one cookie shelf, and it came with PICTURES.

cards.question: Noah has his orders to build an ark. What does God say He will bring upon the earth?
God says everything on the earth will perish in the flood.

cards.text: And then comes the best word in God's whole speech to Noah. "But."

cards.question: Everything on the earth will perish. But what does God say He will establish with Noah?
God tells Noah he will enter the ark. Who goes in with him?

answers.text: His wife and sons and their wives
His father Lamech and his brothers
His sons and all their servants

cards.text: Then God says the animals are coming too. Not to visit, friend. To MOVE IN.

cards.question: God tells Noah to bring ___ of every living creature into the ark, male and female.
How will every kind of bird and animal and crawling creature get to Noah?

answers.text: He must buy them in towns

cards.text: One more thing on the list: every kind of food that is eaten, gathered for Noah's family and the animals. I stress out packing ONE cookie box, and this man is packing for a boat full of animals.

cards.question: Noah has the plans, the animal list and the food list from God. How much of it does Noah do?

answers.text: Most of it with a few changes
Just the ark and nothing more

cards.text: Then the LORD tells Noah it's go time: "Go into the ark, you and all your family". And He tells Noah why.

cards.question: The LORD tells Noah to take his family into the ark. What reason does He give?

cards.text: Now the animal list gets an update, like when the order changes after you already started packing the boxes. For the clean animals and the birds of the air, the number goes UP.

cards.question: How many pairs of every kind of clean animal does Noah take with him?
For every kind of unclean animal, Noah takes just one pair, a male and its mate.

cards.text: Then God gives Noah the timeline. Seven days from now, He will send rain on the earth.

cards.question: Once God sends the rain on the earth, how long will it fall?

cards.text: Noah does all that the LORD commanded, and he's 600 years old when the floodwaters come. Six HUNDRED, friend, and I got a little worn around the edges and ended up in a junk drawer.
Noah's family heads into the ark to escape the flood. And the animals come to Noah two by two, male and female, as God had commanded.

cards.question: Noah's sons go into the ark, but their wives stay behind.

cards.text: Seven days pass, and the floodwaters come, right when God said they would. It's the seventeenth day of the second month, in the six hundredth year of Noah's life.

cards.question: The flood starts on the seventeenth day of the second month. Where does all that water come from?

answers.text: The great deep and the heavens
One huge wave from the sea
A river that overflows its banks

cards.text: The rain falls for forty days and forty nights, and every kind of creature is inside the ark with Noah's family. And I thought keeping six cookie cutters in line on one counter was a JOB.

cards.question: Every creature is inside the ark, as God commanded Noah. Who shuts Noah in?

cards.text: The door is shut. For forty days the flood keeps coming on the earth, and the waters rise.

cards.question: As the floodwaters rise, what happens to the ark?

answers.text: It is lifted high above the earth
It gets stuck deep in the mud
It is broken apart by the waves

cards.text: The waters keep surging and rising, and the ark floats on the surface. And I thought the day the Millers' sink overflowed was a flood.

cards.question: Finally, the waters completely prevail upon the earth. How far up do they reach?

answers.text: Up to the tops of the trees

cards.question: The high mountains are covered. How deep is the water over the mountaintops?

cards.text: Then comes the hard part, friend. Every living thing that moved upon the earth perished: birds, livestock, animals, every swarming creature and all mankind.

cards.question: Every living thing on the face of the earth is blotted out. Who remains?

answers.text: Only Noah and those in the ark

cards.text: And the waters prevail upon the earth for 150 days. We'll leave the ark right there on the water for now, but stick around, friend, because this story is NOT finished.

findings.problem: The joke compares being blameless (a moral quality) with getting flour on his mustache (being messy). These are not the same action, so a stranger could say 'huh?'.

rule.text: 2. The everyday comparison must have the same action.

findings.problem: Card 4 just quoted 'The end of all living creatures has come before Me,' which rules out 'Only the mighty men' and 'Only the great cities.' Both wrong answers also start with 'Only,' so the right answer stands out by its pattern.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'The animals are coming too' gives away the answer to card 15, which asks how the animals get to Noah. The right answer is 'They will come to him.'

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: 'This man is packing for a boat full of animals' says Noah is already carrying out God's commands, before card 17 asks how much of them Noah does. It rules out the wrong answer 'Just the ark and nothing more.'

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 8 of the 10 choice cards are multiple choice, with 1 true or false and 1 fill in the blank. Multiple choice dominates the stop by a wide margin.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.

findings.problem: 'The animal list gets an update' and the comparison 'when the order changes after you already started packing' say that 7:2-3 changes God's earlier instruction in 6:19-20. They also suggest Noah had already started loading animals. The text never says how the two instructions connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: Saying the number goes up only 'for the clean animals and the birds of the air' implies the unclean animals stay at one pair. That gives away card 5, which asks whether Noah takes just one pair of each unclean animal.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: For this 'where' question, the right answer 'The great deep and the heavens' sounds biblical, while the wrong answers sound plain and modern. The wrong answers are also not real details from the Bible. 'One huge wave from the sea' is close enough to 'the great deep' that a baker could argue for it.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.

findings.problem: The joke invents a new backstory event: the day the Millers' sink overflowed. The Millers' kitchen is part of his fixed backstory, not a small moment around his bakery.

rule.text: His own world isn't Bible fact. His backstory, family, bakery and mission are the Dorinverse story in this file. He can talk about them freely, but never adds anything new to them. His jokes can make up small moments and habits around his bakery.

findings.problem: Cards 4 and 5 already established that the mountains were covered, and card 6 said all mankind perished. Together they rule out 'Noah and the mighty men' and 'Those on the highest mountains,' so the question can be answered without reasoning.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: All 4 choice cards in this stop are multiple choice.

rule.text: No formula. Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern. No stop repeats another stop's pattern, and no type dominates a stop by a wide margin.
